purpose: Host integration decisions to carry into the Rust MVP

acceptance: Three new VMs reach cloud-init done without manual guest repairs
Mac key-only SSH and SFTP succeed before and after restart
VM UUIDs and SSH host keys are unique; SSH keys survive restart
Public HTTPS and DNS work; host, LAN router, and another VM are blocked
limits: Current transport is OpenSSH via the host; Iroh remains to be implemented

storage.candidate_layout: Physical ZFS pool -> tenant parent with reservation and hard quota -> Incus-owned child and logical Incus pool
storage.ownership: Only the tenant parent is configured directly; Incus owns its child datasets and volume lifecycle
storage.non_thin_admission: Back configured guest disk sizes, image cache, per-VM metadata, ZFS overhead, and pending operations before allowing a mutation
storage.headroom: Keep a separate unreserved pool accounting floor. An unused dataset reservation is not a substitute. Include all managed global/cache consumers in admission.
storage.quota_reductions: Persist the lower future admission target separately; retain current backing until commitments have actually been released
acceptance: A reaches both its guest filesystem limit and tenant physical cap
A separate quota-capped consumer reaches the remaining admitted global capacity while leaving the accounting floor intact
B fills its guest filesystem with incompressible data and verifies readback without QEMU backing I/O errors
Internal clones survive origin deletion and remain charged to the correct tenant
Restart, deletion, trim, scratch-pool import, and retained reservations behave as recorded
limits: File-backed scratch pool validates accounting and orchestration, not physical-disk failure recovery or performance
A root administrator bypassing accounting can violate the operating floor
Arbitrary user snapshots, thin provisioning, and universal overhead sizing remain deferred
Controller admission, concurrency, and crash-recovery transactions require separate Rust integration tests

cpu.candidate: Root-owned, pre-created per-VM cgroup v2 cpusets; launcher enters the cgroup and sets helper affinity before executing QEMU; Incus pins vCPUs
cpu.allocation: All SMT siblings of a physical core belong to the same VM; stopped VMs retain commitments
cpu.housekeeping: Host services and QEMU helpers have separate housekeeping CPUs; route movable interrupts and unbound workqueues there
acceptance: Effective per-VM cpuset excludes every other VM's dedicated cores
vCPUs remain individually pinned and helpers remain on housekeeping CPUs during concurrent CPU and I/O load
Attempting to set affinity to another VM's core fails at the cgroup bound
Policy applies before QEMU exec and survives restart, stop/start, Incus restart, and host reboot
limits: Residual per-CPU kernel work and hardware interference are not a hard real-time guarantee
The static lab launcher is a prototype; the Rust controller must derive and persist policy from its allocation ledger
The wrapper and AppArmor integration must be version-pinned and retested on Incus/QEMU upgrades

desktop.dependency_policy: Pin mutually compatible releases and commit Cargo.lock
desktop.architecture: GUI uses shared Rust client; allocation and authorization remain server-side
